Judgment

This miscellaneous second appeal under Section 71(6) of Food Safety and Standards Act (in short "FSSA") has been filed against the judgment dated 21/11/2025 passed by Principal District Judge,
Gwalior/Appellate Tribunal in RCA No. 116/2025, as well as order dated 27/12/2024 passed by Additional District Magistrate/Adjudicating Officer, District Gwalior in Case No. Q/Food Safety/113/2024.
2.

According to prosecution case, on 27/9/2023 at about 3:00 pm, the Food Safety Officer, along with his team, carried out the inspection of Jaigurudev Milk Dairy, and during inspection, it was found that 12 kg of paneer, 15 kg of curd, 15 kg of ghee in a container were kept for human consumption and sale.
Since the Food Safety Officer had a suspicion that paneer and dahi might be substandard, therefore, samples were collected.
The samples were sent to the Food Analyst.
The samples were found to be substandard.

Notice was issued to appellant but he did not exercise his power 2 MSA-2-2026 under Section 46(4) of FSSA and Rule 2.4.2(6) of the Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011, and accordingly, a complaint was filed.
A show- cause notice was issued by the Adjudicating Officer.
Appellant denied that any search was carried out.
It was claimed that the samples were not collected in accordance with law, therefore, they were found to be of substandard quality.

3. The Adjudicating Officer, after recording the evidence of parties, came to a conclusion that the paneer and curd were found to be substandard, and accordingly, appellant has violated the provisions of Section 51 of the FSSA and imposed a fine of Rs.2,00,000/-.

sentences.text: Being aggrieved by the order passed by Adjudicating Officer, appellant preferred an appeal before Principal District Judge, Gwalior/Appellate Tribunal under FSSA, and by judgment dated 21/11/2025, the appeal was partly allowed, and while upholding the findings recorded by the Adjudicating Officer regarding violation of Section 51 of FSSA, interfered with the amount of penalty and reduced it from Rs. 2,00,000/- to Rs. 1,00,000/-.
5. Challenging the orders passed by the Adjudicating Officer as well as Appellate Tribunal below, it is submitted by counsel for appellant that appellant is a very small business operator.

6. Heard learned counsel for appellant.
7.
Although in the grounds raised in the memo of appeal it was alleged that there was a delay in conducting the test, but no arguments to that effect were advanced by counsel for appellant.
Merely because appellant is a petty 3 MSA-2-2026 vendor would not entitle him to sell substandard food articles.

8. Under these circumstances, this Court is of considered opinion that no illegality was committed by the Adjudicating Officer as well as Appellate Tribunal by holding that the samples of curd and paneer collected from the shop of appellant were of substandard quality and he did not exercise his right under Section 46(4) of FSSA and did not opt for retesting by a referral laboratory.
9. So far as the question of penalty is concerned, the Appellate Tribunal has already adopted a very sympathetic view by reducing the penalty from Rs. 2,00,000/- to Rs. 1,00,000/-.
Undue sympathy shown to the persons who are involved in sale of substandard food articles is not in the interest of human health.
10. Under these circumstances, no case is made out to warrant any interference.

11. Accordingly, judgment dated 21/11/2025 passed by Principal District Judge, Gwalior/Appellate Tribunal in RCA No. 116/2025, as well as order dated 27/12/2024 passed by Additional District Magistrate/Adjudicating Officer, District Gwalior in Case No. Q/Food Safety/113/2024 are hereby affirmed.
12. The appeal fails and is, hereby, dismissed.

(G. S. AHLUWALIA) JUDGE AKS Prem Singh Rathore vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 23 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168090141/
